sec: The WHVP / FHVP / HVPG table read row by row · p1003

items.q: Match the p1003 table locations with their pressure patterns — 1) Presinusoidal  2) Sinusoidal  3) The row where the hepatic vein cannot be cannulated … A) WHVP increased, FHVP increased, HVPG normal  B) WHVP, FHVP and HVPG all normal  C) WHVP increased, FHVP normal, HVPG increased
items.exp: Presinusoidal: normal/normal/normal; sinusoidal: increased/normal/increased; the unlabeled row: increased / increased (hepatic vein cannot be cannulated) / normal. (Book p1003)

items.q: The prehepatic and presinusoidal rows of the p1003 table are identical: WHVP, FHVP and HVPG are all:
items.exp: Both the prehepatic and presinusoidal rows print Normal in all three columns. (Book p1003)

items.q: In the sinusoidal (cirrhotic) row of the table, WHVP is increased while FHVP remains:
items.exp: Sinusoidal: WHVP increased, FHVP normal, HVPG increased. (Book p1003)

items.q: In a patient with Budd–Chiari syndrome the hepatic vein cannot be cannulated. Which p1003 table row fits this situation, and what does it predict for HVPG?
opts: The unlabeled row — WHVP and FHVP increased, HVPG normal
The presinusoidal row — HVPG normal with all pressures normal
items.exp: The unlabeled row: WHVP increased, FHVP increased (hepatic vein cannot be cannulated), HVPG normal — the pattern of post-hepatic obstruction. (Book p1003)

items.q: ‘In presinusoidal portal hypertension the HVPG is increased according to the p1003 table.’
opts: False — presinusoidal: WHVP, FHVP and HVPG are all normal
False — the WHVP is increased instead
items.exp: Presinusoidal row: normal / normal / normal. (Book p1003)

items.q: In the p1003 flow, an HVPG > 10 mm Hg prompts Rx with the non-selective β-blocker labelled (best):
items.exp: Bracket on the table: > 10 mm Hg → Rx non-selective β-blocker : carvedilol (best). (Book p1003)
